title: A test drive for exchange-correlation functionals on noncollinear magnets: Mn$_3$Ir, Mn$_3$Ge, NiS$_2$, and YMnO$_3$
authors: Marie-Therese Huebsch, Martijn Marsman, Jacques K. Desmarais, Stefano Pittalis, Fabien Tran
abstract: A first-principles description of noncollinear magnets is challenging, and the practical behavior of genuinely noncollinear exchange-correlation approximations is largely untested. Spin-current density-functional theory (SCDFT) admits noncollinear approximations constrained by local U(1)$\times$SU(2) gauge invariance, an exact condition unavailable in the more restrictive framework of spin-DFT (SDFT). Using the Vienna ab initio simulation package (VASP), we compare two recently developed noncollinear SCDFT functionals, NCMSCAN and LFNCBR89-NCCS, against locally collinear SDFT extensions of four common functionals (PZ, PW92, PBE, and SCAN) for several noncollinear $d$-electron systems. The key finding is that among all tested functionals, only the SCDFT functionals recover the spin texture of the experimental ground state of NiS$_2$, and they do so at a cost comparable to standard semi-local approximations. Yet the two SCDFT functionals differ in equilibrium volumes, band gaps, and on-site magnetic moments. Overall, this survey illustrates the usefulness of SCDFT in capturing noncollinear physics with the tested approximations.
summary: This paper tests advanced theoretical methods for calculating the electronic structure of noncollinear magnets using first-principles DFT. By comparing Spin-Current DFT (SCDFT) against simpler Spin-DFT approaches, the authors demonstrate that SCDFT is necessary to accurately capture the complex spin textures observed in materials like $	ext{NiS}_2$. The findings establish SCDFT as a powerful, albeit complex, tool for modern magnetism research.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing and rigorously testing exchange-correlation (XC) approximations for describing noncollinear magnetism, as genuinely noncollinear approximations are largely untested in practice.
main_result: The study finds that only Spin-Current DFT (SCDFT) functionals successfully recover the spin texture of the experimental ground state for $	ext{NiS}_2$, demonstrating SCDFT's utility in capturing noncollinear physics.
method: The authors employed first-principles calculations using the Vienna ab initio simulation package (VASP), comparing two SCDFT functionals ($	ext{NCMSCAN}$ and $	ext{LFNCBR89-NCCS}$) against locally collinear extensions of standard functionals ($	ext{PZ}$, $	ext{PW}92$, $	ext{PBE}$, $	ext{SCAN}$).
model_or_system: The research focuses on four noncollinear $d$-electron antiferromagnetic magnets: $	ext{Mn}_3	ext{Ir}$, $	ext{Mn}_3	ext{Ge}$, $	ext{NiS}_2$, and $	ext{YMnO}_3$. The theoretical framework involves solving the Generalized Kohn–Sham (GKS) equations incorporating spin-current density dependence.
key_observables: Equilibrium lattice constants, electronic band gaps, on-site magnetic moments ($\mu_x, \mu_y, \mu_z$), and the recovery of the experimental spin texture.
important_parameters: The theoretical constraint of $	ext{U}(1)	imes	ext{SU}(2)$ gauge invariance is crucial for the SCDFT functionals.
main_assumptions: The comparison highlights that while SCDFT captures noncollinear physics, the tested functionals do not uniformly reproduce all experimental observables with higher accuracy than their locally collinear counterparts.
figures_summary: Figure 1 contrasts the local collinear (SDFT) and noncollinear (SCDFT) calculation frameworks. Table VII compares the computational costs (SCF steps and time) of various functionals across the tested materials.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the theoretical framework, contrasting the restrictive local projection of Spin-DFT with the gauge-invariant approach of Spin-Current DFT. It then applies this framework to calculate and compare structural, electronic, and magnetic properties for the four target materials.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it pushes the boundaries of electronic structure theory for magnetic materials, providing advanced computational tools (SCDFT) necessary for modeling complex, non-collinear magnetic ordering that is central to modern condensed matter physics.
